title: The zero-ship halt counts within one batch in memory, so wave next batches of one wave (wave.max_cycles 1) never trip it
summary: Found in the PR #1049 review. zeroShipHalt (go/cmd/evolve/cmd_loop_zeroship.go) keeps its wave tally on the batch coordinator (b.zeroShip) and runs only in prepareIteration, before each wave. The console launches every wave with evolve wave next, whose default wave.max_cycles is 1 (go/internal/policy/policy_wave.go), so each batch runs one wave and the tally starts empty each time. A boundary re-exec resets it too. The compiled breaker of operating-policy.md section 4.1 therefore never fires in normal operation, and the rule rests on the operator alone.
fix: Count zero-ship waves across batches from durable evidence (runs/ outcomes grouped by wave, or the wave records of evolve wave), check after each wave as well as before it, and acknowledge a halt through the resolved-fingerprints ledger, as the no-work-handoffs rule does since PR #1049.
acceptance: A loop test with max_cycles 1 run as two consecutive batches, each with a zero-ship wave, halts with LOOP_ZERO_SHIP_HALT after the second wave
Consuming the halt's P0 item, or evolve loop --reset --fingerprint, acknowledges the run so the next batch does not halt again on the same waves
operating-policy.md section 4.1 and runtime-reference.md describe the cross-batch window
